Voznesensk Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaivska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. According to local historian Boris Sokolov, this cemetery dates to the second half of the 19th century; during WWII, German forces destroyed it and used its gravestones to build the Bolgarskiy bridge over the Mertvovod River. The Jewish community here had grown remarkably dense by 1910, supporting seven synagogues, before wartime occupation from August 1941 led to the execution of over 3,000 people from the region, most of them Jewish. A small Jewish community of 48 people remains in Voznesensk today.
